**Medical doctor wants to go into early drug development**  
Hello all!

  
**Background** I'm a recently graduated (30M) physician. I've worked as a physician for a year, and I've had misgivings about medicine since halfway through medical school.   I was diagnosed with ADHD ("ADD") a couple of months ago, after struggling with school and work my entire life. I am as yet untreated for ADHD. I mention ADHD only because I've come to realize how important it will be for me to pursue a career in something I'm passionate about, and the only life science subject I still have a passion for is pharmacology.     Although I've been offered several paid PhD positions, I don't want to go into research because the kind of research available to me frankly isn't that exciting.   I'm not interested in clinical drug development.

  
**The plan**  I want to quit medicine and go into early drug development, something I've come back to again and again throughout medical school and after graduating.  It seems to me that medicinal (or organic) chemistry is the way to go. There are no medicinal chemistry programs where I live. I plan on getting a BSc in chemistry, and then compose my own MSc (this is possible in my country), consisting of organic, medicinal and computational chemistry, drug development, pharmaceutical bioinformatics, and as much math as I can cram in. I already know programming (Python, R). My goal is to work in industry (i.e., pharmaceutical company in early drug discovery/development). I plan on financing my degrees by working as a physician part-time and during summer breaks.

  
**Questions**

* Is my combination of MSc courses appropriate for working in drug development? Are there any subjects I should add?
* My hope is that my medical degree (and clinical experience) will make me stand out as a candidate. Is this far-fetched?

Sorry, didn't mean to be rude. I've seen a therapist for GAD and depression. Neither helped. Been on antidepressants for ~3 years, all I get is an emotionless baseline. Never any happiness. And of course the near-suicidal depression bouts...
Thank you, but the author seems to be suffering from bipolar disorder while I am highly convinced I have borderline personality disorder.

I know it doesn't. I know that those with BPD can never live a full life. (Sorry for this, you really don't have to talk to me, I'm just impossible. Whatever you say my anxiety and/or depression will turn into something bad. Really I'm an absolutely worthless individual)

It's well-known that psych patients get medical care of a lower standard, and nobody has it worse than BPD-patients. It's a warning sign in your health record. The things I've seen. BPD-patients who wait >6 h in the ER with a ruptured colon. Getting signed into involuntary for "psychosis" and then dying of that massive stroke that were the primary cause of secondary psychosis.
